summary: The public evidence supports a concrete implementation pattern: parse a machine-friendly git diff first, normalize each file into status plus hunks plus exact old/new line ranges, and then expand review only into a bounded dependency neighborhood instead of the whole repository. The clearest implementation references are open source: reviewdog shows how to filter diagnostics to added lines, diff context, or changed files, and Qodo's PR-Agent shows diff-hunk-centered review with dynamic context expansion, token-aware compression, and incremental narrowing to files changed since the previous review. Proprietary vendors point in the same direction: GitHub Copilot and CodeRabbit both document PR-scoped review with optional repository-wide context, but they do not publish the exact neighborhood-selection heuristics. One important correction to the proposed UX is that PR-style branch scope should usually default to `main...HEAD`, not `main..HEAD`, because triple-dot follows the merge base.

findings.claim: Use `git diff --name-status -z` or raw diff output as the first parse stage so changed files are classified before hunk analysis; Git exposes stable status codes such as A, D, M, and R and NUL-safe output for scripting.
findings.evidence: The manual documents `--name-status`, `--diff-filter`, and `-z`; raw/name-status output exposes per-file change kinds and script-safe path termination.

findings.claim: Exact changed line ranges should come from unified diff hunk headers, and each diff line should be mapped to old/new line numbers during parsing.
findings.evidence: reviewdog parses `@@ -oldStart,oldLen +newStart,newLen @@` into hunk fields, then assigns `LnumOld` and `LnumNew` as it walks added, deleted, and context lines.

findings.claim: If the UX means “review what this branch changed since it diverged from main,” default to `main...HEAD`; `main..HEAD` is an endpoint diff and is not the same thing.
findings.evidence: Git's examples show `topic..master` as the same endpoint comparison as `topic master`, while `topic...master` means changes since the branches split.

findings.claim: Changed-file-plus-neighbors is a standard incremental-analysis pattern, not an exotic idea.
findings.evidence: CodeChecker explicitly says: "Only the changed files and its dependencies need to be reanalyzed."

findings.claim: A robust incremental review cache must invalidate on more than file hashes; cross-file dependencies and analyzer configuration changes also matter.
findings.evidence: SonarQube says reuse depends on conditions including cross-file dependencies, quality profile setting changes, and build setting changes.

findings.claim: For PR review, it is practical to skip unchanged files entirely when the language allows independent file analysis and to reuse target-branch cache otherwise.
findings.evidence: SonarQube says pull-request analysis reports only issues on new code, and its incremental-analysis docs describe skip-unchanged-files plus target-branch cache use for PR analysis.

findings.claim: Qodo's public PR-Agent docs scope analysis around PR diff hunks but also load the full contents of modified files and PR metadata, not just raw patch text.
findings.evidence: The metadata stage lists PR title, description, commit history, PR diff patches, and the entire content of modified files as review inputs.

findings.claim: Qodo/PR-Agent widens hunk context by code structure, not only by a fixed number of surrounding lines, which is a practical model for dependency-neighborhood review.
findings.evidence: The docs describe an asymmetric and dynamic context strategy that can extend toward an enclosing function or class.

findings.claim: Large-PR handling should treat deletions differently from additions and modifications; a useful pattern is to deprioritize deletion-only hunks and carry deleted files separately.
findings.evidence: Qodo's compression strategy says to prioritize additions over deletions, remove deletion-only hunks, and keep a separate deleted-files list.

findings.claim: Qodo's open-source GitHub provider implements incremental review by locating the previous review comment, computing the commit range since that time, and restricting files to those changed in that range.
findings.evidence: The provider loads the previous review, computes `commits_range`, and fills `unreviewed_files_set` from files in the new commits.

findings.claim: PR-Agent's reviewer prompt is intentionally diff-scoped: it tells the model to review new code in PR diff hunks and to avoid speculation outside visible changed segments.
findings.evidence: The prompt says to focus on new code added in the PR diff and reminds the model that it only sees changed code segments.

findings.claim: reviewdog is a strong reference implementation for diff-aware filtering: it supports `added`, `diff_context`, `file`, and `nofilter`, and its core data structure is a path-to-line map built from parsed hunks.
findings.evidence: The implementation defines four filter modes and populates per-file line maps from each hunk's `LnumNew` values before deciding whether a diagnostic should be reported.

findings.claim: GitHub Copilot scopes review to pull-request changes but can widen into repository context, and it can be configured to re-review every new push.
findings.evidence: GitHub documents full project context gathering for code review and an automatic-review trigger that can run on every new commit pushed to the PR.

findings.claim: CodeRabbit publicly positions its review flow as PR-scoped first and incremental afterward, with repository-wide context available through full-repo analysis and code-graph analysis.
findings.evidence: CodeRabbit says later commits receive incremental reviews focused on new changes, and its overview advertises code-graph analysis across the project.

findings.claim: CodeRabbit's architecture docs confirm that its comments are not derived from a bare diff alone; it clones the full repository and runs agentic exploration plus specialized agents.
findings.evidence: The architecture page says reviews run with the full repository cloned, agentic exploration, and multiple specialized agents.

findings.claim: Java already has a dependency-neighborhood tool suitable for impacted review: `jdeps` can emit dependency graphs and also answer reverse-dependency questions.
findings.evidence: Oracle documents `--dot-output` for graph export and `--inverse` for artifacts that directly and indirectly depend on a matched node.

findings.claim: For JavaScript and TypeScript, dependency-cruiser is a practical graph builder and rule engine for caller/callee neighborhood expansion.
findings.evidence: Its README describes validating and visualizing dependencies and shows DOT graph generation with `--output-type dot`.

findings.claim: For JavaScript and TypeScript, Madge directly supports reverse-neighborhood lookup through dependents, which is useful when a changed file is deleted or its exports change.
findings.evidence: Madge documents `.depends()` as returning all modules that depend on a given module and `.dot()` for graph output.

findings.claim: If you need a custom multi-language graph builder, Tree-sitter supports efficient incremental reparsing, which makes graph invalidation cheaper after small edits.
findings.evidence: Tree-sitter's advanced parsing docs say reparsing with the old tree creates a new tree that internally shares structure with the old one.

artifacts.description: Reference pipeline for batch diff-aware review with dependency-neighborhood expansion and incremental invalidation.
artifacts.content:
base = git_merge_base(target_branch, head)
files = parse_name_status_z(`git diff --name-status -z --find-renames ${base} ${head}`)
hunks = parse_unified_diff(`git diff --unified=0 --find-renames --no-ext-diff ${base} ${head}`)
changed = join(files, hunks)
for file in changed:
  if file.status == ADDED:
    scope[file] = full_new_file(file) + outbound_dependencies(file) + inbound_dependents(exported_symbols(file))
  elif file.status == MODIFIED:
    scope[file] = touched_hunks(file) + enclosing_symbols(file) + callers(file) + callees(file)
  elif file.status == DELETED:
    scope[file] = reverse_dependents(deleted_path=file.path) + references_to_deleted_symbols(file)
  elif file.status in {RENAMED, COPIED}:
    scope[file] = treat_as(path_change + semantic_change)
impacted = graph_expand(changed.files, hops=1)
dirty = changed.files union impacted union cache_invalidate(content_hash, graph_version, ruleset_version, prompt_version)
review_input = build_prompt(changed, scope, cached_summaries, commit_messages, PR_metadata)
run_review(review_input)

artifacts.description: Minimal command set for branch-scoped review input generation.
artifacts.content:
git diff --name-status -z --find-renames main...HEAD
git diff --numstat -z --find-renames main...HEAD
git diff --unified=0 --find-renames --no-ext-diff main...HEAD
# Use main..HEAD only when you intentionally want endpoint diff, not merge-base PR scope.

artifacts.content: {"CodeRabbit":{"documented_scope":"PR review on open; incremental review on later commits; full repository clone; code-graph analysis","precision":"high-level vendor description"},"GitHub Copilot":{"documented_scope":"code changes plus additional relevant context; optional full project context gathering; optional review-new-pushes","precision":"official but high-level"},"Qodo/PR-Agent":{"documented_scope":"PR diff hunks + modified-file contents + PR metadata + dynamic context + token-aware compression + incremental commit-range narrowing","precision":"official docs plus source code"},"reviewdog":{"documented_scope":"diagnostics filtered to added lines, diff context, changed file, or no filter","precision":"implementation-level open source"}}

gaps: No public documentation from CodeRabbit, GitHub Copilot, or Qodo Merge describes the exact dependency-neighborhood expansion algorithm, hop limit, or ranking logic for callers versus callees.
Exact proprietary handling of added files versus deleted files versus renamed files inside vendor review models is mostly undocumented; public docs describe capabilities, not detailed heuristics.

Qodo's current docs surface open-source PR-Agent mechanics clearly, but the linked `incremental_update` page appears unavailable, so incremental behavior had to be inferred from source and adjacent docs.
I did not find a recent, vendor-neutral benchmark that isolates the benefit of diff-only review versus diff-plus-dependency-neighborhood review using a reproducible open-source pipeline.
escalations: Change the planned CLI default from `--diff main..HEAD` to `--diff main...HEAD`, or offer both and make the semantic difference explicit in help text.
Choose language-specific graph backends early; callers/callees are not a single generic primitive across Java, JS/TS, Python, Go, and mixed-language repos.
Treat cache invalidation as a first-class design problem: include file content hash, graph-builder version, parser version, ruleset version, and prompt version in cache keys, not just the diff.
Do not assume vendor-scoping claims imply true dependency-aware impact analysis; for proprietary tools, that part is still largely an inference from high-level docs.
